prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle graphene, opening the field of moire quantum matter.

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a rare case in which a sharp theoretical prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model, 2011, flat bands at a specific twist angle) was followed by an unambiguous experimental discovery (correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018) in a clean, tunable system. It created a new field, moire quantum matter, that now covers fractional Chern insulators, other twisted and moire heterostructures and new routes to engineering correlated and topological states. This fits the committee's order of work: the discovery first, then the people behind it. The theory-plus-experiment structure maps onto three names, and the discovery has been reproduced by many groups over eight years. Nature gave a clue here, in the form of a surprising observation, and theory had already pointed at the right place.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity and attribution. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated, and the field is young compared with the others on the list. Attribution is also hard: Yuan Cao and other experimental co-authors, the Dean and Young groups, and earlier theory on twisted bilayers (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) fall outside the three credited names, and the committee may judge that a prize now would cut across contested priority. Moreover the quantum-matter space already received recognition through the 2016 topological-phase prize and graphene in 2010.

responses.point: Pearce ranks the twisted-graphene candidate last of his eight and calls it intermediate in maturity, because the pairing mechanism is unresolved and waiting a few years would clarify consequences.
responses.response: I take the point about the superconducting mechanism, but the Nobel question is whether the discovery is secure, not whether every interpretation is settled. The prediction and the observation of correlated and superconducting states are reproduced in many laboratories and extended to other moire systems. Gravitational-wave background evidence, which Pearce ranks third, is a weaker case on the same maturity test, since the individual arrays are at the 3-4 sigma level and the source is not identified. I would not apply the maturity criterion more strictly to B017 than to B004.

responses.point: Kroll puts the optical lattice clock first as a clean two-person prize for Katori and Ye, with 10^-18 precision, many confirming labs and a pending redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I agree the credit is clean and the maturity high, and that is why I keep B015 as my first alternative. My reservation is about originality of the underlying step: the field builds on the frequency comb and ion-clock prizes of 2005 and 2012, and the 2025 and 2022 prizes have also leaned on quantum metrology and optics. A prize for B015 would reward a very deep refinement of precision, whereas moire graphene opened a new regime of physics. I do not claim that is decisive, and if the committee values clean attribution above all, B015 is an honourable choice.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks Kane-Mele-Molenkamp topological insulators first and B017 third with only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, treating Bistritzer's contribution as joint with MacDonald.
responses.response: I understand why he trims to two, since the Bistritzer-MacDonald paper is a joint work and two is the cleaner pairing. But the prediction paper has two authors and Bistritzer is the first, so omitting him in a prize on that prediction would be hard to defend, and the three-name limit leaves room. I share his admiration for B051 and rank it third, but the allocation between 2D and 3D parts (Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Molenkamp, Hasan) is more tangled than in B017, and 2016 already honoured topology in matter.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first on conceptual originality and technological reach, but notes that the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits and a second prize in the same family needs justification.
responses.response: His timing caveat is serious and I agree with it: B012 is mature, but a prize immediately after the 2025 award on superconducting circuits invites the charge of repetition. I do not see the same difficulty for moire graphene, which he also ranks second and describes as secure and timely. This is a point on which our views converge rather than differ, and I would prefer to see B012 considered later.

uncertainties: Whether the credited names are the right three, given the role of Yuan Cao and other experimental co-authors and of the competing experimental groups.
Whether the committee would rather wait for the superconducting mechanism to be clarified.
Whether the clean attribution and the strong majority first-place support for B015 outweigh the larger conceptual novelty of B017.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile: my work is in string theory, gravitation and cosmology, and I have no documented connection to any of the shortlisted candidates or their institutions.
